verdict.rationale: Alloy documents its own transaction-monitoring workflows. They evaluate transaction events in real time or on a schedule, apply policy logic and raise alerts when thresholds are met, and events can be routed to Source Workflows for monitoring. However, no evidence shows thresholds being set per customer segment or describes the compliance-officer rule-configuration experience. Missing for 10: documented segment-specific threshold configuration, detail on rule authoring for compliance users, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a compliance-officer, I can configure transaction monitoring rules and segment-specific thresholds

citations.quote: Monitors transaction events in real time or at scheduled times to detect suspicious activity, apply policy logic, and generate alerts or investigations when thresholds are met.
Workflows can run in real time as part of a Journey evaluating an incoming application, or on a schedule as a Portfolio workflow
any event can be submitted for additional monitoring by mapping the event type to a Source Workflow.
Alloy supports dozens of use cases like interdicting on transactions
